outlook.statement: The three-wheeler segment in India is at an inflection point. Rural demand is recovering. Urban last-mile logistics is growing rapidly. The government's push for electric mobility is creating a structural tailwind that benefits companies with existing EV infrastructure - of which Atul Auto is now firmly one. We enter FY27 with expanded capacity, a fully integrated EV division, a strengthened balance sheet and a team that has proven its ability to execute at pace.

International strategy for FY27 and beyond is focused on deepening partnerships in existing markets while entering new territories in South-East Asia and East Africa, regions where the last-mile transportation gap is large and growing.
Domestic growth strategy is centred on expanding the EV portfolio's reach in semi-urban corridors and deepening penetration of the CNG segment in metro-adjacent markets.

India's growth outlook remains upbeat, anchored by strong domestic consumption, infrastructure investment, and services exports; the Union Budget for FY26-27 raised public capex to a record ₹12.2 lakh crore, focused on rural connectivity, road building, railways and logistics, which are expected to significantly boost demand for mobility solutions.
The Company will focus on improving man-machine productivity to raise overall output, while continuing to build on the sales momentum, margin gains and network expansion achieved during the year.

EV penetration expected to rise further to around 9.5-10% in FY27, helped by extended PM E-DRIVE incentive window for three-wheelers; 29 states/UTs had notified dedicated EV policies as of December 2025, with 4 more in draft stages.

The integration of the acquired L5 Electric Vehicle business with the Company's existing operations is expected to generate operational and commercial synergies through optimization of manufacturing capabilities, dealership network, after-sales service infrastructure and marketing efforts. The transaction is also expected to enhance operational efficiency, improve market reach and create a seamless ecosystem for electric vehicle manufacturing and distribution.
KAFL will continue to play a vital role in strengthening the retail-financing ecosystem for the Company's products and contribute to the sustainable growth of the business.

The management is taking necessary measures to improve operational performance, optimize costs and capitalize on emerging opportunities in both domestic and international markets for Atul Greentech Private Limited.
Atulease Private Limited is planning to commence its business in near future for operational leasing of three-wheeler and other vehicles.

The Company is investing further in people and equipment so as to strengthen its R&D and thereby enhance its capability to achieve better position in the future. In the future, we will continue following more innovative, environment friendly and practical automobile vehicles considering changes in market trends.

The Ahmedabad Facility is capable of meeting the Company's existing manufacturing requirements as well as having enough space available to enhance the production capacity with minimum capex to meet anticipated demand for the next several years.

Consolidating manufacturing operations at a single location is expected to improve operational efficiency, optimize utilization of manpower and resources and reduce operating and administrative costs.

risks: Raw Material & Battery Input Cost Risk: Volatility in steel, lithium-ion cell and battery raw material prices (cobalt, lithium) could raise production costs and pressure margins
Currency & Import Dependence Risk: Rupee depreciation increases the cost of imported battery cells and electronic components used in EV models
Regulatory & Policy Risk: Changes to EV incentive schemes (PM E-DRIVE, EMPS) or emission norms could alter near-term demand and product economics
Competitive Intensity Risk: Entry of larger two- and four-wheeler OEMs into the electric three-wheeler space could intensify pricing pressure and erode market share
Demand Concentration Risk (Rural/Semi-Urban): Heavy reliance on rural and semi-urban markets makes sales sensitive to monsoon outcomes, agri-income cycles and rural credit availability
Financing & Credit Availability Risk: A large share of buyers depend on vehicle financing; tighter lending conditions or rising interest rates could slow retail sales
Technology Transition Risk: Slower-than-expected localisation of EV technology could leave the Company at a cost or product disadvantage versus faster-moving peers
Infrastructure Risk (Charging Network): Uneven charging infrastructure outside major cities could slow EV adoption in the Company's core rural and semi-urban markets

Geopolitical risk: Prolonged or wider conflict in West Asia impacting energy prices and shipping routes; renewed trade tensions and supply chain fragmentation; high public debt levels eroding fiscal buffers across major economies
Crude oil price volatility impacting input costs, logistics expenses, and consumer demand for vehicles
